words:
## Goal
Tend must never claim a seed is ready for intake solely because its first line declares confirmation.

## Evidence
F1 in research #167: a real TEST seed confirmed with Seed Me and edited afterward is called ready by Tend while Shape correctly reports changed confirmation contents. Operator request: "Run the documentation checks including the new files, then implement the false-readiness fix with a regression test."

## Scope and boundaries
Conservative fix: file-only discovery yields an explicitly unchecked seed stage, not verified readiness. The shared Seed Me boundary owns its name, label, continuation eligibility and next step. Tend says seed needs checking and directs the operator to Seed Me; Shape's existing helper-backed verification remains the only seed-ready claim. Keep cheap discovery, no helper-per-session scan, no new verifier or source writes. Preserve copying and opening Shape for the unchecked stage. Do not fix incomplete discovery (#167 F2), process lifetime (F3), stale return (#165), or add selected-detail verification in this slice.

## Done when
- [ ] A header-only or changed confirmed seed never becomes seed-ready in Tend.
- [ ] The unchecked stage has a clear next step; copying/Shape remain available without writes or model calls.
- [ ] A regression using a real CI-pinned Seed Me confirmation, altered seed and actual terminal catches the false claim; both 100x30 and 80x24.
- [ ] Shared-boundary unit regression covers absence of verification; verified Shape positive and negative journeys remain passing.
- [ ] Important regressions fail with the old readiness claim restored, then pass after restoration of the fix.
- [ ] Design/maps reflect the narrower guarantee; full zero-call checks and observed counts reported.
